Dive in

The work

Closing the gap between authority and empathy

Many women rise into power while quietly negotiating a gap — between what leadership asks of them and who they actually are.

This studio closes this gap with practice, precision, honest feedback and the company of women who get it.

How do you lead with full conviction while remaining unmistakably yourself?

How do you hold standards, complexity and humanity — without becoming a bitch, a witch or a nurse?

How do you grow authority that feels lived, not performed?

That's the work.

What we work on

Being read, constantly.

At the highest level, competence is rarely the question. What senior women navigate is something more particular: being read constantly. In how they enter a room, hold pressure, set direction, and carry responsibility through uncertainty. This studio works with that visibility.

Over three days, a small group of senior women work in real time through conversation, feedback, field experiences, and shared tables. We bring together boardroom judgement, intentional presence, humanistic leadership, and artistic expression.

The work is precise. You examine how your values translate into visible leadership signals. You develop boundaries that protect your integrity and practice the kind of recognition that makes genuine empathy possible, even when the stakes are high.

The aim: authority that is clear, grounded, and fully inhabited. Authority that carries weight and feels unmistakably your own.

Location

Venice will shift your perspective.

Venice has dealt with the constraints of leadership in the most extraordinary way and remained beautiful, unique and true to its own founding values. This is why, over the course of three days, we will deep dive into the Venetian presence. Conversations will unfold across hidden courtyards, workshops, long tables, boats and spaces. The Venice Authority Studio believes that this very unique location provides the different vantage points needed to shift perspectives.

The pace changes. Attention changes. You change.

Because perspective rarely shifts inside familiar routines.

What you leave with

Five things that stay.

01

Your Authority Signature

You leave with a clear personal stance on what you build, protect and prioritise. You sharpen the language you use in openings, boundaries, disagreement and decision moments, so your authority becomes more visible, more coherent and more recognisably yours.

02

Boardroom Credibility

You leave with a stronger sense of how you are read in high-level rooms and how to communicate with greater precision, timing and weight. You work on stakeholder dynamics, sponsorship, influence and the strategic relationships that shape what becomes possible.

03

Decisions Under Pressure

You leave with a practical structure for moments that require clarity, speed and consequence. You learn how to hold pressure without losing presence, how to communicate difficult decisions and how to repair trust when it matters.

04

Humanistic Leadership in Practice

You leave with a deeper understanding of leadership as relationship. How people move with you. How trust forms. How resistance speaks. How recognition can become a turning point. You practice authority that holds standards while remaining deeply human.

05

Presence and Voice

You leave with tools to steady yourself before the room reads you. You work with voice, rhythm, pace, silence and the visible signals that communicate seniority. You develop a short reset for meetings, negotiations and moments of visibility.

Atmosphere

The vibe.

Some of the most important conversations do not happen in formal rooms. They happen over dinner, on the walk back, across a table, in the quiet after someone says something true.

Meals are part of the studio because shared tables create a different kind of intelligence. A small group of remarkable women, gathered in Venice, speaking honestly about power, visibility, work and life.

This is where insight becomes personal. This is where recognition happens. This is where the work deepens.

Who this is for

Women who lead where visibility has consequences.

Director · VP · C-Level · Partner · Founder

This studio is for senior women at Director, VP, C-level, Partner or Founder level who operate where decisions matter and visibility has consequences. It is for women who carry responsibility with intelligence and care. Women who value honest feedback, precise practice, meaningful conversation and the company of peers who understand what it means to lead at a high level.

This is a room for women who have already achieved a great deal. Women who want their authority to feel as good as it looks from the outside.

8

participants maximum · By application only

Format

Three days in curated locations across Venice.

Before the studio

Personal Calibration

Each participant has a personal calibration call of thirty to forty-five minutes — before the studio begins.

During the studio

Three Days in Venice

Applied labs, field experiences, real-time feedback, one high-stakes simulation, shared meals and guided conversations across curated locations.

After the studio

Implementation

Participants join three implementation case sessions and a peer pod for continued momentum, accountability and honest exchange.

The Team

We built this studio because it didn’t exist. And we think it should.

We are four practitioners from different disciplines: strategy, neuroaesthetics, humanistic leadership and art. We created this studio because authority needs more than method. It needs judgement, presence, human depth, aesthetic intelligence and the courage to be fully expressed.

Boardroom Readiness Delphine Mousseau

Delphine Mousseau has built and run businesses at a scale most people only advise on. She doubled Tommy Hilfiger’s European e-commerce business and launched it across 22 markets. At Zalando as a VP with a team of 200 she oversaw a €5bn operation across 17 countries. In 2018 she stepped deliberately off the executive track and built something else entirely.

  • Board member: Aramis Group, Safestore, refurbed (listed and growth-stage)
  • Former NED Fnac Darty; advisory boards: Decathlon, Flaconi
  • Chaired remuneration and nomination committees across multiple mandates
  • Founder, Rising Pineapples — community advancing women across industries
In this studio, she brings what very few can: the real experience of leading at the highest level, with strategic clarity, boardroom judgement and a presence that is formidable and human in equal measure.
Visible Authority Lisa Maria Pippus

Lisa Maria Pippus works at the intersection of aesthetic psychology, perception and leadership. Trained in fashion in Toronto and Milan, she is the creator of the Visual Language System™ — a framework for understanding how visual choices shape impact and influence before a word is spoken.

  • Creator of the Visual Language System™
  • Clients include Tommy Hilfiger, Zalando, Bayer Pharma, Freshfields
  • Two decades working with senior executives on presence, coherence and visibility
  • Known for helping leaders align external expression with values and ambition
In this studio, she makes the invisible visible — so that how you are seen finally matches who you are.
Humanistic Leadership Petra Ronzani

Petra Ronzani has spent over fifteen years in senior leadership roles at some of Europe’s most demanding cultural institutions. She now researches humanistic leadership at the University of Hildesheim and works as a mediator and strategic consultant accompanying organisations through transformation and change. Raised in Germany with Italian and Croatian roots, shaped by her studies of Chinese language and culture, she brings deep intercultural intelligence to her work.

  • Senior leadership: Haus der Kunst Munich, Bavarian State Opera, Münchner Kammerspiele, Berliner Volksbühne
  • Doctoral researcher, University of Hildesheim — humanistic leadership
  • Mediator and strategic consultant: change, conflict, transformation
  • Board member, SALOON Venice and Berlin — feminist and artistic networks across Europe
In this studio, she works on what she believes most deeply: that authority, when genuinely expressed, has a beauty of its own — and that this becomes possible when leadership is truly human.
Creative Courage Mamiki

Mamiki came to art by way of another life entirely. For years she operated at the highest levels of global brand strategy. The decision to leave, to begin again, to find a language that fits — that trajectory is precisely what she brings into the room. Her work now explores what becomes possible when people stop performing and begin expressing themselves fully.

  • Senior executive career with Nike and Tommy Hilfiger — global brand strategy at scale
  • Artist and art therapist
  • Known for helping people reconnect with voice, instinct and personal power
  • Harnesses energy as a strategy
In this studio, she works on the one thing that carries a room: the presence that comes from knowing exactly who you are — and letting it show fully.
